claims.text: Do (●): length/height and weight; BMI; blood pressure; developmental surveillance; behavioral/social/emotional screen; depression and suicide risk screen.
claims.locator: Periodicity Schedule p. 1 chart, column "20 y": ● in rows Length/Height and Weight, Body Mass Index, Blood Pressure, Developmental Surveillance, Behavioral/Social/Emotional Screening, Depression and Suicide Risk Screening; chart key

claims.text: Risk assessment (★), act if positive: vision; tobacco, alcohol or drug use; anemia; tuberculosis; STIs.
claims.quote: = risk assessment to be performed with appropriate action to follow, if positive
claims.locator: Periodicity Schedule p. 1 chart, column "20 y": ★ in rows Vision, Tobacco, Alcohol, or Drug Use Assessment, Anemia, Tuberculosis, Sexually Transmitted Infections; chart key

claims.text: Within its age range (↔): hearing (●); dyslipidemia (●); HIV (●); hepatitis B (★ risk assessment); hepatitis C (●); sudden cardiac arrest/death (★ risk assessment).
claims.quote: = range during which a service may be provided
claims.locator: Periodicity Schedule p. 1 chart, column "20 y": inside the range arrows of rows Hearing, Dyslipidemia, HIV, Hepatitis B Virus Infection, Hepatitis C Virus Infection, Sudden Cardiac Arrest/Death; chart key

claims.text: Hearing: audiometry including 6,000 and 8,000 Hz once between 11 and 14, once between 15 and 17, and once between 18 and 21 years.
claims.quote: 10. Screen with audiometry including 6,000 and 8,000 Hz high frequencies once between 11 and 14 years, once between 15 and 17 years, and once between 18 and 21 years.

claims.text: Substance use: CRAFFT (crafft.org) is a recommended tool; with concern for substance or opioid use, consider recommending or prescribing naloxone.
claims.quote: A recommended tool to assess use of alcohol, tobacco and nicotine, marijuana, and other substances, including opioids is available at http://crafft.org. If there is a concern for substance or opioid use, providers should consider recommending or prescribing Naloxone

claims.text: Depression and suicide risk: screen adolescents, making every effort to preserve their confidentiality.
claims.quote: Screen adolescents for depression and suicide risk, making every effort to preserve confidentiality of the adolescent.

claims.text: Tuberculosis: test on recognition of high-risk factors, per the AAP Red Book.
claims.quote: Tuberculosis testing per recommendations of the AAP Committee on Infectious Diseases, published in the current edition of the AAP Red Book: Report of the Committee on Infectious Diseases. Testing should be performed on recognition of high-risk factors.

claims.text: STIs: screen adolescents per the AAP Red Book.
claims.quote: Adolescents should be screened for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) per recommendations in the current edition of the AAP Red Book

claims.text: HIV: screen at least once between 15 and 21, preserving confidentiality; after that, retest youth at increased risk annually or more often.
claims.quote: Screen adolescents for HIV at least once between the ages of 15 and 21, making every effort to preserve confidentiality of the adolescent, as per “Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection: Screening” (https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/ recommendation/human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-infection-screening); after initial screening, youth at increased risk of HIV infection should be retested annually or more frequently

claims.text: Hepatitis C: screen everyone at least once between 18 and 79; those at increased risk (including past or current injection drug use) are tested and reassessed annually.
claims.quote: All individuals should be screened for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection according to the USPSTF (https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/ recommendation/hepatitis-c-screening) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommendations (https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/69/rr/rr6902a1.htm) at least once between the ages of 18 and 79. Those at increased risk of HCV infection, including those who are persons with past or current injection drug use, should be tested for HCV infection and reassessed annually.

claims.text: Sudden cardiac arrest/death: risk assessment as appropriate, per the AAP report on sudden death in the young.
claims.quote: Perform a risk assessment, as appropriate, per “Sudden Death in the Young: Information for the Primary Care Provider”

claims.text: Immunizations: every visit is an opportunity to update and complete them.
claims.quote: Every visit should be an opportunity to update and complete a child’s immunizations.
